header.running_head: 3. The Rights and Duties of Muslims

blocks.tamil_translation: said, “Give up committing sin.” The sinful man asked, “Leave me with my Lord” (it is between me and my Lord); “were you sent to watch over me?” The (angered) worshipper said, “By Allah! Allah Ta'ala will not forgive you” or “Allah Ta'ala will not admit you into Jannah.” After that, when both of them died, they were brought together before Allah Ta'ala (in the world of souls) where souls gather. Allah Ta'ala asked that worshipper, “Did you know beforehand (that I would not forgive)? Or (you argued with him that Allah would not forgive! While forgiveness lies in My hands), did you have the power to stop Me from forgiving him?' To that sinner, “Go to Jannah by My mercy! (because he had placed his hope in the mercy of Allah) “Take this worshipper to Jahannam!” Allah Ta'ala commanded the angels.” Hazrat Abu Hurairah (RA) narrates that he heard Rasulullah ﷺ say this.

blocks.text: Explanation:- The meaning of this hadith is not that one may boldly commit sins; that sinner was forgiven only by the immense mercy of Allah Ta'ala. It is not the rule that every sinner will be dealt with in this way, because the rule is that sin is punished. Nor does it mean that sins and things forbidden in the Deen should not be stopped.
